idiom_name: Notification object + Error entries + checks that append instead of throwing
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: create one notification per operation; give it an add(Error) operation, a hasErrors() predicate and a read accessor for the collected entries; let each independent check append an entry rather than throw or return early; return the notification (or a result type carrying it) to the caller, which renders or routes every entry and proceeds only when none is present. Keep the entries as data - code, field or path, severity and an optional message - so they survive serialisation across a process boundary and can be translated in the presentation. Short-circuit checks whose input depends on an earlier check, and reserve exceptions or panics for conditions that are not expected outcomes.
code_sketch:
note = Notification.new()
check_seats(note, request)      # appends, never throws
check_date(note, request)       # independent of the previous check
return response(note)           # caller reads note.errors / note.hasErrors
pitfalls: Returning the notification but leaving the check to the caller's memory: an unchecked result silently accepts invalid input.
Dependent checks executed unconditionally, so a follow-up check runs on a value that failed to parse.
One shared mutable notification reused between interactions, leaking errors across requests.
Entries that carry only prose, so the caller cannot map an error back to the offending field.
